newsitem.title: USA: Continental to buy 30 Boeing jets.
newsitem.headline: Continental to buy 30 Boeing jets.

text.p: Continental Airlines Inc. said Tuesday it has signed a letter of intent to buy 35 widebody aircraft from Boeing Co. through the year 2004 and to buy additional Boeing aircraft over the next 20 years.
Terms of the agreement were not disclosed. Based on list prices, the order is worth about $3 billion.
Continental officials were not available for comment.

The airline, the nation's fifth-largest, said the order consists of five Boeing 777-200 aircraft and 30 767-400ER aircraft, with options for additional 777 and 767 purchases to be negotiated in the future.
The deal is in addition to five 777 aircraft which the Houston-based airline already has on order with Boeing.
The total of 10 777 aircraft will be delivered in September 1998 through May 1999. The 30 767 aircraft will be delivered in mid-2000 through the end of 2004.

The new widebody aircraft will replace Continental's fleet of six DC10-10 and 31 DC10-30 aircraft, which will be retired as the new Boeing aircraft are delivered. They will also be used to expand the airline's international and transcontinental service, it said.
